what: Here’s why Slate changed the battery in its cheap EV truck

clean_source_blocks.text: A lot has changed since electric vehicle startup Slate Auto unveiled the prototype of its first vehicle just over a year ago. But despite volatile gas prices and the rising cost of new cars, the Slate Truck is now official—and it has landed within the company’s targeted price range. As much attention as Jeff Bezos’s backing of Slate Auto has received, the truck’s electric powertrain and value proposition may be what really resonated with potential buyers. Slate says more than 180,000 people have decided that the promise of an affordable, reliable, and customizable vehicle was worth a $50 reservation. “Slate gives customers the freedom to buy only what they need today and personalize their vehicle as their needs change tomorrow,” Slate CEO Peter Faricy said in today’s announcement.

Slate Auto is developing the cheapest new electric pickup truck on the market. It's also set to beat the Ford Maverick for the position of cheapest truck and the Nissan Leaf for the title of cheapest EV of 2026. Slate Auto's new pickup truck is innovative and different than most new vehicles from major automakers in many ways. Here's how it compares to the cheapest pickup trucks of 2026. The Ford Maverick ($26,771) is the most affordable new pickup truck model you can buy in 2026 until Slate's EV hits the streets. It's followed by the Hyundai Santa Cruz ($29,750), another small truck model. Ford's Maverick is a standard hybrid and the Santa Cruz is a gas-powered model.

The new Slate Truck will start at $24,950, making it the only new pickup truck model in 2026 with a price under $25,000. It also happens to be a fully-electric model, which is another huge distinction. EVs tend to be more expensive than their gas and hybrid counterparts because of their unique designs. Nissan's Leaf ($29,990) will be the second-most affordable new electric vehicle when the pickup arrives. The Slate Truck is significantly smaller than the Ford Maverick and Hyundai Santa Cruz. Ford's tiny truck model is 199.8 inches long. Hyundai's Santa Cruz is just 195.7 inches long. Slate's Truck is the smallest of the trio at 174.6 inches long.

Slate Auto's truck is a two-seater, but buyers can customize the EV for an additional fee to make it suitable for five as an SUV. Its small body and simplistic, no frills design help keep production costs low, allowing the automaker to produce such an affordable vehicle. The Slate Truck uses a 150 kilowatt single rear-mounted motor to produce 201 horsepower and 195 pound-feet of torque, which is adequate for its size. The standard battery allows for 205 miles of driving range. This isn't much range by today's standards, but a smaller, less powerful standard battery is another factor in the EV's attractive pricing. Additionally, drivers willing to develop a regular charging regimen can easily work around the base model's low driving range. Slate's small truck model is compatible with North American Charging Standard (NACS) chargers for DC fast charging.

payload.title: Slate Auto tuo alle 25 000 dollarin sähköavolavan Yhdysvaltain markkinoille
payload.summary: Slate Truck on tulossa Yhdysvaltain vuoden 2026 automarkkinoille poikkeuksellisen edullisena sähköavolavana. Mallin hinta alkaa 24 950 dollarista, ja yhtiön mukaan yli 180 000 ihmistä on tehnyt 50 dollarin varauksen.
payload.content:
Slate Auto on julkistanut Slate Truck -sähköavolavan virallisena mallina noin vuosi prototyypin esittelyn jälkeen. Uutuuden lähtöhinta on 24 950 dollaria, mikä asettaa sen vuoden 2026 edullisimpien uusien avolavojen joukkoon ja tekee siitä samalla poikkeuksellisen halvan täyssähköauton Yhdysvaltain markkinoilla.

## Edullisuus on mallin keskeinen lupaus

Slate Truckin hinta jää alle 25 000 dollarin, mikä erottaa sen monista nykyisistä sähköautoista. Vertailukohtina mainitaan Ford Maverick, jonka hinta on 26 771 dollaria, sekä Hyundai Santa Cruz, jonka hinta on 29 750 dollaria. Nissan Leafin hinnaksi mainitaan 29 990 dollaria, joten Slate pyrkii haastamaan myös edullisimpien sähköautojen kärkeä.

Yhtiön mukaan kiinnostus on ollut vahvaa: yli 180 000 ihmistä on tehnyt 50 dollarin varauksen. Slate Auto korostaa mallin ideana sitä, että asiakas voi ostaa ensin vain tarvitsemansa auton ja muokata sitä myöhemmin omien tarpeidensa mukaan. Toimitusjohtaja Peter Faricy kuvasi julkistuksen yhteydessä auton antavan asiakkaille vapauden ostaa vain sen, mitä he tarvitsevat nyt, ja personoida ajoneuvoa myöhemmin.

## Pieni koko ja yksinkertainen rakenne pitävät hintaa alhaalla

Slate Truck on selvästi pienempi kuin osa sen edullisista kilpailijoista. Sen pituudeksi kerrotaan 174,6 tuumaa, kun Ford Maverick on 199,8 tuumaa ja Hyundai Santa Cruz 195,7 tuumaa pitkä. Perusmalli on kaksipaikkainen, mutta ostajat voivat lisämaksusta muokata sähköauton viisipaikkaiseksi katumaasturiksi.

Teknisesti mallissa on yksi taakse sijoitettu 150 kilowatin sähkömoottori. Se tuottaa 201 hevosvoimaa ja 195 paunajalkaa vääntöä. Vakiomallin toimintamatkaksi ilmoitetaan 205 mailia, mikä ei ole nykyisten sähköautojen mittapuulla erityisen paljon, mutta pienempi akku auttaa pitämään hinnan matalana.

Auto tukee North American Charging Standard -pikalatausta, joten se on yhteensopiva NACS-latureiden kanssa. Slate Auto näyttää rakentavan mallin tarkoituksella yksinkertaiseksi ja muokattavaksi vaihtoehdoksi ostajille, joille matala hankintahinta on tärkeämpi kuin suuri koko tai pitkä toimintamatka.

Slate says more than 180,000 people have decided that the promise of an affordable, reliable, and customizable vehicle was worth a $50 reservation. “Slate gives customers the freedom to buy only what they need today and personalize their vehicle as their needs change tomorrow,” Slate CEO Peter Faricy said in today’s announcement.

Slate Auto is developing the cheapest new electric pickup truck on the market. It's also set to beat the Ford Maverick for the position of cheapest truck and the Nissan Leaf for the title of cheapest EV of 2026. Slate Auto's new pickup truck is innovative and different than most new vehicles from major automakers in many ways. Here's how it compares to the cheapest pickup trucks of 2026. The Ford Maverick ($26,771) is the most affordable new pickup truck model you can buy in 2026 until Slate's EV hits the streets. It's followed by the Hyundai Santa Cruz ($29,750), another small truck model. Ford's Maverick is a standard hybrid and the Santa Cruz is a gas-powered model.

The new Slate Truck will start at $24,950, making it the only new pickup truck model in 2026 with a price under $25,000. It also happens to be a fully-electric model, which is another huge distinction. EVs tend to be more expensive than their gas and hybrid counterparts because of their unique designs. Nissan's Leaf ($29,990) will be the second-most affordable new electric vehicle when the pickup arrives. The Slate Truck is significantly smaller than the Ford Maverick and Hyundai Santa Cruz. Ford's tiny truck model is 199.8 inches long. Hyundai's Santa Cruz is just 195.7 inches long. Slate's Truck is the smallest of the trio at 174.6 inches long.

Slate Auto's truck is a two-seater, but buyers can customize the EV for an additional fee to make it suitable for five as an SUV. Its small body and simplistic, no frills design help keep production costs low, allowing the automaker to produce such an affordable vehicle. The Slate Truck uses a 150 kilowatt single rear-mounted motor to produce 201 horsepower and 195 pound-feet of torque, which is adequate for its size. The standard battery allows for 205 miles of driving range. This isn't much range by today's standards, but a smaller, less powerful standard battery is another factor in the EV's attractive pricing. Additionally, drivers willing to develop a regular charging regimen can easily work around the base model's low driving range. Slate's small truck model is compatible with North American Charging Standard (NACS) chargers for DC fast charging.
